svg.text: MAVIA processing pipeline
From the uploaded course outline to the learner’s adaptive walk through the learning path, with the tool or algorithm used at each step
Extraction / content (groupmate)
Questions + answers (user)
Grouping / versions / path / publish (shared)
Learner-facing adaptive serving
STAGE
TOOL / ALGORITHM
Course outline uploaded (PDF)
The teacher uploads the syllabus / course outline.
Parsed into a topic tree: CourseGroup + OutlineNode rows
(module > lesson > topic), which become the course skeleton.
PyMuPDF (fitz) embedded-text, table and column extraction
Regex line normalisation + noise filter (drops “table of contents”,
“quiz”, “semester”, schedule/admin rows) — outline_parser.py
Image-only PDF: pages rendered at 2× and transcribed by the
Ollama vision model (IMAGE_DESCRIPTION_MODEL, default gemma3:4b)
Lesson PDFs uploaded and routed to a topic
One or more lesson PDFs per topic. Each file is matched to the
outline node it teaches (or the teacher’s pick is validated),
so several PDFs can cover the same topic from different books.
TF-IDF vectoriser + cosine similarity (scikit-learn) over the
outline node text vs. the PDF text — content_generator.py
Thresholds: MATERIAL_TOPIC_COSINE_THRESHOLD 0.08,
broad-match ratio 0.60, max 3 broad matches
Extraction → ordered LearningObject rows
Each PDF becomes an ordered list of learning objects:
title, the section heading it sat under, content, order.
Text blocks, instructional tables and meaningful figures
are separated; the teacher then confirms the objects per file.
PyMuPDF block / table / image extraction; borderless-table
region detection; captioned-figure region finder
Instructional-content classifier splits teaching prose from
chrome (instructional_content_classifier.py)
Definition splitting + title refinement heuristics (regex)
Figure description (audio-first requirement)
A figure has no text a blind learner can hear, so its content
is written as a description and becomes the object’s content.
Ollama vision model gemma3:4b via /api/generate
ROLE / TASK / CONTEXT / FORMAT prompt, no-preamble rule,
2–4 sentences (6 max), surrounding lesson text as context
(incl. the overleaf passage) — image_describer.py + disk cache
Grouping → concepts (one bundle per PDF)
Objects from different PDFs that teach the same thing become one
LearningObjectGroup. A group IS a concept, and a concept is one
step of the learning path. Inside it, each PDF keeps an ordered
bundle, so the same lesson chunked coarsely and finely still lines up.
Runs inside a PDF: consecutive objects sharing a section heading
(unit_matching.find_units) — structure alone over-merges
Cross-PDF corroboration required: a matching heading or title
Scoring: sentence-transformers all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings +
cross-encoder/stsb-roberta-base rerank (pinned revisions, cached)
≥ 0.60 with margin → grouped automatically; 0.30–0.60 → teacher card
Images additionally need label corroboration (AI descriptions share
stock phrasing and score 0.6+ regardless of subject)
Teacher review of connections
“Review Connections” screen: give an object its own concept, move it
into another concept, or reorder it inside its own PDF’s block.
Teacher decisions are never overwritten by a later automatic pass.
Derived bundles — concept_bundles.bundles_for_group() is the single
authority for ordering (no bundle table)
Provenance flags on the group: teacher / llm_validated / heuristic;
label_locked and rejected suggestions outrank every automatic path
Content versions per concept
One PDF supplies the Normal version; every other PDF’s contribution
is classified Simplified / Elaborated / Extra. A missing version is
generated. A supplied version stores no copied text — it IS its objects.
LLM version classifier over the group’s members (Ollama gemma3:4b,
OLLAMA_MODEL) — course/version_classifier.py
Readability check: Flesch–Kincaid grade level, word count as tie-break
(course/readability.py) validates simpler vs. more elaborate
Gap filling: Gemma writes the missing version → LessonVariant rows,
one per object of the Normal bundle (course/variant_generator.py)
Question + answer generation per concept
A draft bank is generated from the concept’s Normal bundle text, then
checked against the topic’s own PDF text by a corrective-RAG grounding
gate. A draft the source does not support is deleted and its rejection
reason is fed back into a bounded corrective regeneration pass.
Survivors are classified, deduplicated and trimmed, then saved as
GeneratedQuestion rows (MCQ and True/False).
Why the gate exists
Measured on the first published topic before it: 61 of 76 questions
used words absent from every PDF, and two marked “plasma” correct
where the source says “gas” and “solid”. The source was in the
prompt both times — so this checks compliance, not availability.
Retrieval is scoped to the topic’s own materials: a global index
would validate a question against text the learner never heard.
1 · Draft
Ollama llama3.2:3b (QUESTION_LLM_MODEL), streaming /api/generate with a
JSON schema constraining the decode; temperature 0.7, one call per
thinking order (LOT/HOT) with the format mix requested inside it, plus
few-shot examples. Overgenerates in the same call rather than re-calling.
Parsing: fence strip + balanced-span salvage; structural validation
rejects unusable answers — services/question_generator.py
2 · Grounding gate (corrective RAG) — services/grounding.py
a. Lexical: content words absent from the topic corpus → reject
(deterministic, no model; inflections folded so “depicted” meets “depicts”)
b. Retrieve: draft Q&A as query → all-MiniLM-L6-v2 cosine over raw
PDF text in 90-word overlapping chunks, top-K (QUESTION_VALIDATION_TOP_K)
c. Judge: QUESTION_JUDGE_MODEL at temperature 0, schema-constrained →
supported / contradicted / unsupported, naming the answer the source backs
Failures deleted; reasons appended to the prompt for a bounded retry
(QUESTION_VALIDATION_MAX_RETRIES). Encoder or judge unavailable → the
verdict records “unverified” rather than passing silently.
Audio generation
Every object and every version gets a spoken track, including the
alternate PDF’s own track — a silent lesson is a functional defect.
Edge TTS (en-US-AriaNeural, EDGE_TTS_VOICE), retry wrapper,
per-object MP3 clips played in bundle order — audio_generator.py
Needs network access to speech.platform.bing.com
Publish gate
Publishing runs in order and refuses rather than shipping a broken
lesson: describe missing figures → settle versions → completeness
check → audio → learning path. Any failure leaves the topic unpublished.
run_topic_publish() phase runner with a live event stream to the UI
Completeness check: concepts_missing_a_version()
The path is saved only when every earlier phase succeeded, so the
saved path always matches what learners can reach
Learning path derived over concepts
A prerequisite graph over the topic’s concepts, then a linear order
saved as LearningPathStep rows (position + prerequisite links).
This is the gold-standard-tested core of the thesis.
Three criteria, each voted, 3/3 accepted · 2/3 pending · else nothing:
· Temporal order — position in the merged document order (Wang 2016)
· Semantic reference, RefD-style — share of A’s key terms that B uses,
plus head-word mention and section containment (Liang 2015);
key terms via document-frequency pruning (REF_MAX_DF_RATIO 0.34),
phrase match by all-MiniLM-L6-v2 cosine ≥ 0.80
· Foundationality — inbound/outbound ratio (MIN_IOL_MARGIN 0.25)
Vetoes: contrast words (“unlike”, “while”, “than”); coordinate siblings
need a naming reference; Examples concepts take no pair, ordered last
Linearisation: Kahn’s algorithm (topological sort) over accepted edges
Learner interaction — adaptive path mode
The mobile learner walks the published path by step position, hears
the concept, answers its questions, and is re-taught or re-routed on a
miss. Mastery is tracked per concept; nobody is ever stranded.
Steps by position, questions from GeneratedQuestion (Bloom level,
thinking order) via the published path payload — one LOT + one HOT per step
Mastery: Bayesian Knowledge Tracing — _bkt_update() with p_guess,
p_slip, p_learn, starting mastery and ceiling from AdaptiveConfig
On a miss, in order: content ladder normal → simplified → elaborated;
detour to the nearest prerequisite (bounded by MAX_REMEDIATION_DEPTH and
one detour per step); switch to the concept’s alternate PDF chunk;
one second ladder pass for a step with no structural remedy; then advance
(adaptive/services.py, path mode — legacy flat mode still exists)
Scope note
DQN is manuscript- and notebook-only. The reinforcement-learning work lives in notebook/mavia_rl/ (environment, agent, training, evaluation) and is
NOT wired into Django serving; step 12 is BKT plus the deterministic re-teach ladder.
